turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Checkout flow. Nearly missed the submit button. It barely registered visually — took a moment to find the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "nearly missed the submit button", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The visual hierarchy is inverted, with the secondary "Continue Shopping" action appearing more prominent than the primary "Place Order" action.
B) The "Place Order" button is visually buried or de-emphasized compared to the surrounding content and the other button.
C) The placement of the buttons at the very bottom of the layout makes them easy to overlook during a scan of the page.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What kind of work situation typically brings you to a screen like this? When does this task usually come up for you?
turns.a: Group purchase. Deadline. I'm executing the final action on behalf of others. Primary CTA needs to be obvious — no searching required.

turns.q: What specific confirmation were you hoping to see from that button's appearance regarding the finality of the order?
turns.a: Find and execute the primary CTA on the first scan. One look, one action. Not search and re-read to confirm it's available.

turns.q: What specific visual cues on the "Place Order" button would signal to you that it is the definitive final step? How would a successful redesign make that priority immediately obvious upon first glance?
turns.a: Said it. Obvious CTA, no hunting, confirmation appears.

turns.q: Looking at the "Place Order" button specifically, is it the lack of a solid color fill that makes it blend in, or is the text color too similar to the background?
turns.a: 'Place Order' is obviously the primary action — high contrast, clearly visible, reads as active. One look, execute, reach confirmation. No ambiguity about whether the button is available or where to find it.

turns.q: If you were to describe the "Place Order" button's border and fill in simple terms, would you call it a solid block of color or an outlined shape with transparent space inside?
turns.a: 'Place Order'. Hard to find. Wasn't obvious it was there.

turns.q: Comparing the "Place Order" button to the other button on the screen, does it look like it has a solid background color while the other one is just an outline, or are they both styled the same way?
turns.a: 'Place Order' has disabled-state styling: gray fill on gray background, 12px label — no contrast, no visual weight. That's the barrier. Users don't execute buttons that look unavailable. Fix: solid high-contrast fill — brand color with white label text, WCAG AA compliant (4.5:1 for the label text). Label at ≥14–16px. Primary CTA needs to read as active and prominent. Right now it reads as inactive and invisible. One button, three CSS properties. That's the barrier and the fix.
